rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so the table is shifted toward stronger obfuscation while respecting the hot-loop nature of this TSVC Searching-dbl kernel: the 40KB 'init' function and search loops dominate execution, so BCF and FLA get high SecurityGain but mid-range RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights to concentrate bogus control flow and flattening where features favor them without blanket application to the hottest loops; SUB and SPLIT are cheap, low-risk transformations applied broadly (high Security/Diversity, low cost weights) to break arithmetic and basic-block patterns; IBR adds indirect branching on the now-larger CFGs with moderate runtime weight; ICALL hides call targets across the 14 small functions cheaply; and IGV gets high DiversityGain with elevated CorrectnessRisk weight so global-variable encoding is applied selectively given this kernel's heavy reliance on shared arrays. Since round 1 showed no ICE or miscompiles, CorrectnessRisk weights stay low-to-moderate overall, accepting somewhat more size growth against the ~43KB baseline.
